Example for downloading and running from the command line on Mac:

```
curl -L -O 'https://github.com/KhronosGroup/glTF/releases/download/v1.0-draft/collada2gltf_mac_v1.0-draft_x64.gz'
gunzip collada2gltf_mac_v1.0-draft_x64.gz
mv collada2gltf_mac_v1.0-draft_x64 collada2gltf
chmod +x collada2gltf
./collada2gltf
```

uikit 1.0

![uikit-1-0](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/799afd7f-1bf7-4787-a67a-3ff3137492e5) > 1.0 is now officially out ## 4 Major Advantages 1. Breaking changes to be more aligned with html/css meeting developers where they are 2. vanilla three.js - `pmndrs/uikit` - is now the stable core of the project simplifying the adoption across the three.js ecosystem 3. All kits and icon packages are now available as React Three Fiber and vanilla three.js version 4. Simplified architecture to improve maintainability while the project and its use cases mature ## What has changed for developers? Uikit 1.0 introduces several new properties such as `zIndex`, `display: contents`, `white-space`, `classList`, and ìmportant`. It aligns more closely with HTML/CSS behavior through property inheritance, improved styling APIs, and consistent naming conventions. Unnecassary components like `Root` and `FontFamilyProvider` are deprecated and can be replaced by simpler Container patterns and unified style management. Obsolete features, including `opacity`-specific properties, `useRootSize`, and `isInteractionPanel`, have been removed in favor of an API more aligned with HTML/CSS. The full list of changes and the guide for migrating to uikit 1.0 can be found [here](https://pmndrs.github.io/uikit/docs/migration/from-version-0).

Added the capability to load PlayCanvas compressed .PLY files and SPZ compressed .PLY files. Additionally fixed some bugs with rendering spherical harmonics.
- build: add tvOS support (`appletvos`/`appletvsimulator`), Metal-only, via `./build.sh -p tvos`

## 2.4.0 (Oct 19, 2026)

Bug fixes and improvements

### Enhancements

- Add SPZ v4 read support (#484) (@udwinj, @mrxz) 
- Decouple and abstract paged splat load logic from `PagedSplat` into `FetchSource` that retrieves data from in-memory file, URL or any other custom mechanism (#463) (@mrxz, @xohm
, @oscarlorentzon)
- Switch to `flate2` from `zlib-rs` backend for RAD deflate compression. ~50% faster compression, ~2-5% smaller outputs and ~20% faster decoding (#474) (@mrxz, @oscarlorentzon)
- Replace `miniz_oxide` with `flate2` for Gzip (de)compression of SPZ files. Remove `miniz_oxide` as dependency (#485) (@mrxz)
- Address stutter during animations. Skip unnecessary splat sortings if the splat buffer needs or has changed like for example when LoD levels change or splats animate / move (#347) (#460) (@oscarlorentzon, @mrxz)
- Refactor `PagedSplats` into its own separate file (#462) (@mrxz)
- Remove outdated Github workflows CI commands (#464) (@mrxz)
- Add Rust linter (#414) (@mrxz)
- Improve tests (#483, #482) (@mrxz)
- Improve docs (#478) (@oscarlorentzon)

### Bug Fixes

- (WebXR) Use camera projection projection matrix to calculate LoD pixel limit. The THREE.Camera fov value was incorrectly used before: It doesn't match the one reported by the WebXR API (#488) (@oscarlorentzon)
- Adress view-dependent color precission loss due to unwanted SH coefficinets clamping (#465) (@oscarlorentzon) 
- Dispose the LoD index textures when renderer is disposed (#479) (@oscarlorentzon)
- Fix issue with Level 3 Spherical Harmonics (sh3) dropped due to incorrect type assertions. It introduces explicit types in `PackedSplats` and `ExtSplats` instead of loose types + assertions. (#467) (@mrxz, @oscarlorentzon)
- (WebXR) Fix issue with splat size and anti-alias blur rendered at half the correct width. Use whole viewport width for calculations instead of half (#487) (@oscarlorentzon)
- Ignore errors / rejections after `SparkRenderer` is disposed. This can happen when for instance there's pending LoD sorting in parallel in the worker when the renderered is disposed (#476) (@oscarlorentzon)
- Replace workers that hit a fatal error / crash / trap. The pool tried to reuse those in a broken state (#480) (@oscarlorentzon)
- Fix issue with long thin splats drawn off axis, too wide or too narrow. Compute 2D covariance eigenvectors without cancellation (#486) (@oscarlorentzon)
- Stop retrying a failed level of detail tree on every update (#477) (@mrxz, @oscarlorentzon)
- Address raycasting precission and speed issues (#469) (@n3ur0m4n, @oscarlorentzon)

We have another set of bug fixes, some backported from v10. Here are the highlights:

- Portal memory leaks have been fixed. The portal's root state would get held by the parent even when the portal got unmounted disallowing garbage collection. You mount and unmount on a complex enough app and this adds up quickly. A portal can now be cleaned up properly when unmounted.
- Pixel ratio updates automatically when moving between displays or zooming. Note: `setDpr` is overwritten by the `dpr` prop whenever the `Canvas` rerenders. If you want to use `setDpr` then don't use the `dpr` prop. This behavior will change in v10.
- TypeScript JSX types fixed, preventing `React.ElementType` props from collapsing to `never`. Importing R3F no longer breaks unrelated React types.
- Dragging stays active when an object’s `args` change.
- Removed objects disappear immediately with `frameloop="demand"` instead of lingering as ghosts.

This release adds experimental **inkbleed** antialiasing to `@rive-app/webgl2`, along with angular (sweep) gradients, artboard paints, and a handful of fixes.

# New

### Inkbleed antialiasing (WebGL2 only)

Inkbleed is a new antialiasing mode in the Rive Renderer, offered as an alternative to MSAA. Opt in when creating the Rive instance:

```ts
import { Rive } from "@rive-app/webgl2";

const r = new Rive({
  canvas,
  src: "my-file.riv",
  enableInkbleed: true,
});

// Toggle at runtime (only works if enabled at construction)
r.inkbleed = false;
```

Notes:
- It disables the canvas's native MSAA.
- Fills that don't use the clockwise fill rule are converted to clockwise on a best-effort basis; worth checking for visual differences
- Edges bleed out by about half a pixel, which is most noticeable on thin strokes.
- It doesn't apply when using the shared offscreen renderer (`useOffscreenRenderer: true`).

## Other additions
- Angular (sweep) gradients
- Painting with an artboard (artboard as a paint source)
- String template data binding converter
- Text input now blurs when pressing outside the focused field

# Fixes

- Deferred / GPU Canvas: only replay a canvas's last frame per session frame, and back a canvas before a paint samples its image
- Mesh buffers now sync when a mesh samples a canvas image
- Scripts without pointer handlers no longer block pointer hits
- Variable font cache is cleared when the base font is null
- Backwards states entered at their forward twin's end now play correctly
- GL storage-texture polyfill fixes on Mali GPUs

# Performance

- Several renderer improvements: pixel bounds, cubic chopping, stroke cusps, per-verb path counts, draw sort ties
- Text layout is solved once per change; runtime advance and keyframe apply are cheaper
